guideTitle: The Best Chair Mats for Carpet, Including Medium and Extra-High Pile
metaTitle: Best Chair Mats for Carpet: Low, Medium and High Pile (2026)
metaDescription: Most carpet chair mats only cover low pile. We compared eight vinyl, polycarbonate, glass and woven mats, including options rated for medium and extra-high pile.
introParagraphs: Most chair mats sold for carpet are rated only for low pile, under about 1/4 inch. That leaves few options if your carpet is thicker or sits on heavy padding, where a thin flexible mat is more likely to sink and crack.

This guide covers the range: low-pile vinyl, a polycarbonate mat for medium pile, two commercial-grade ES Robbins mats (one rated for extra-high pile over 1 inch), two tempered glass mats and a woven rug-style mat. Rigid glass and composite mats sit on top of the pile rather than relying on a pile rating, though their listings don't give one.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, pile ratings, certifications and warranties, not hands-on testing.

hon-office-chair-mat-low-pile-lip.summary: A 2.2mm PU vinyl mat with anchor bars, ramped edges, a lip and a five-year warranty.
hon-office-chair-mat-low-pile-lip.description:
The HON mat is the sensible choice for standard low-pile carpet: its anchor bars grip pile up to 1/4 inch, its ramped edges and extended lip let the chair roll on smoothly, and it has a five-year warranty.

It is 2.2mm PU vinyl, 36 x 48 inches, with an anti-skid top, and it has an extensive base of buyer feedback.

It is rated for low pile only, and the ES Robbins mats offer lifetime warranties at higher prices.
pros: Low price for a five-year warranty
cons: Thinner than the ES Robbins mats
hon-office-chair-mat-low-pile-lip.skipIf: Your carpet is thicker than 1/4 inch; the GORILLA GRIP or ES Robbins mats are rated higher.

muarts-crystal-clear-heavy-duty.badge: Best Rigid Mat for Heavy Loads
muarts-crystal-clear-heavy-duty.summary: A rigid 5mm, 54 x 32-inch mat rated for 1,400 lb, for carpet or hard floor.
muarts-crystal-clear-heavy-duty.description:
The MuArts is the rigid option for heavy chairs: its 5mm sheet is rated for 1,400 lb, the highest here, and stays flat instead of flexing into the pile.

It measures 54 x 32 inches, works on carpet or hard floor and has a 12-month warranty.

The listing doesn't give a pile rating, so check it suits your carpet. It has no lip, is only 32 inches deep and is heavier to move than vinyl.
muarts-crystal-clear-heavy-duty.bestFor: Heavy chairs, or a setup that may move to a hard floor.
muarts-crystal-clear-heavy-duty.skipIf: You want a stated pile rating; the ES Robbins mats list theirs.

gorilla-grip-slip-resistant-polycarbonat.summary: A flat-shipped polycarbonate mat with spikes, rated for pile up to 3/4 inch.
gorilla-grip-slip-resistant-polycarbonat.description:
The GORILLA GRIP is the lower-cost route to medium pile: it is rated for medium or low pile up to 3/4 inch, and ships flat rather than rolled.

It is 0.087-inch polycarbonate, 36 x 48 inches, with hundreds of spikes on the underside.

It has no lip and isn't rated for high or extra-high pile.
pros: Medium-pile rating at a moderate price
cons: Warranty not stated in the listing summary
gorilla-grip-slip-resistant-polycarbonat.bestFor: Medium-pile carpet at a standard desk.
gorilla-grip-slip-resistant-polycarbonat.skipIf: You need a large area or lifetime warranty; the ES Robbins EverLife covers both.

es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile.summary: A 60 x 72-inch vinyl mat for medium pile, GREENGUARD certified, with a lifetime 'No Crack' warranty.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile.description:
The ES Robbins EverLife covers the largest area here by far: 60 x 72 inches, enough for an L-shaped desk or a lot of rolling. It is rated for medium pile up to 3/4 inch.

It is 0.13-inch vinyl with rounded AnchorBar cleats rather than sharp spikes, made in the USA, GREENGUARD certified and covered by a lifetime 'No Crack' warranty.

It was the most expensive mat here with a listed price at the time of writing, and buyer feedback is less positive than for most mats here, which is worth reading before you buy.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile.bestFor: Large or L-shaped desks on medium-pile carpet.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile.skipIf: You only need a standard 36 x 48-inch area; the GORILLA GRIP covers medium pile for less.

es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.summary: The only mat here rated for extra-high pile over 1 inch including padding, with a lifetime warranty.
es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.description:
The ES Robbins Extra High Pile mat is the one to choose for thick or heavily padded carpet: it is the only mat here rated for pile over 1 inch, including padding.

It is 0.2-inch vinyl, 36 x 48 inches with a lip, with AnchorBar cleats. It is GREENGUARD Gold certified, listed as phthalate- and cadmium-free, made in the USA and covered by a lifetime warranty.

Buyer feedback is the least positive here, so read recent reviews, and at 36 x 48 inches it covers a standard area only.
specs: Pile rating: extra-high, over 1" incl. padding
es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.skipIf: Your carpet is low pile; the HON costs about half as much.

lorell-tempered-glass-chairmat.summary: A 6mm tempered glass mat rated for 1,000 lb and any floor type, with a five-year warranty.
lorell-tempered-glass-chairmat.description:
The Lorell is the glass mat with the strongest buyer feedback here: 6mm tempered glass, 46 x 36 inches, rated for 1,000 lb and, according to Lorell, for any floor type including carpet.

Glass sits rigidly on top of the pile rather than depending on cleats, is scratch-resistant and easy to clean, and has a five-year warranty.

Availability and price on this listing vary, so check the current price. Glass is heavy to move, and 36 inches of depth is modest.
lorell-tempered-glass-chairmat.bestFor: A long-term rigid mat on carpet of uncertain pile height.
lorell-tempered-glass-chairmat.skipIf: The listing is unavailable or expensive when you shop; the GLSLAND is the alternative.

glsland-tempered-glass-chair-mat.summary: A 5mm tempered glass mat rated for 1,200 lb, with four anti-slip pads.
glsland-tempered-glass-chair-mat.description:
The GLSLAND is the lower-cost glass option: 5mm tempered glass, 36 x 46 inches, rated for 1,200 lb, with four anti-slip pads and use on carpet or hard floor.

It is listed as BPA-free, phthalate-free and odorless.

Its pads grip more lightly than cleats, and it's slightly smaller than the Lorell.
glsland-tempered-glass-chair-mat.bestFor: A glass mat on a moderate budget.
glsland-tempered-glass-chair-mat.skipIf: You want a longer stated warranty; the Lorell lists five years.

anji-mountain-rugd-jacquard.summary: A jacquard-woven polyester mat over a PVC core that looks like a rug, for low pile or hard floors.
anji-mountain-rugd-jacquard.description:
The Anji Mountain Rug'd is the mat for a room where a plastic sheet would look out of place: it is jacquard-woven polyester over a PVC core, and looks like a rug.

It is 0.25 inches thick, 36 x 48 inches, with felt backing and rubberized non-slip dots, and it is water- and stain-resistant. Anji Mountain describes it as hand-crafted.

It is rated for low pile or hard surfaces only, and a woven surface may not roll as freely as smooth vinyl.
specs: Construction: jacquard polyester over PVC core, 0.25"
Floors: low pile or hard surfaces
pros: Works on low pile or hard floors
cons: Woven surface may roll less freely
anji-mountain-rugd-jacquard.bestFor: Living rooms and bedrooms where the mat is on display.
anji-mountain-rugd-jacquard.skipIf: Your carpet is medium pile or thicker; the GORILLA GRIP or ES Robbins mats are rated for it.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Low pile (up to about 1/4 inch): HON, Anji Mountain. Medium (up to 3/4 inch): GORILLA GRIP, ES Robbins EverLife. Extra-high (over 1 inch including padding): ES Robbins Extra High Pile.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Consider rigid mats for uncertain pile
buyingCriteria.explanation: Glass and the MuArts rigid sheet sit on top of the carpet. Only the Lorell lists 'any floor type'; the others don't give a pile rating.
Most mats here are about 36 x 48 inches; the ES Robbins EverLife is 60 x 72 for large or L-shaped setups.
The ES Robbins mats carry lifetime warranties and GREENGUARD certification; HON and Lorell list five years.

faq.q: Is there a mat for extra-high pile carpet?
faq.a: Yes. The ES Robbins Extra High Pile mat is rated for pile over 1 inch, including padding, the only one here.

faq.q: What's the difference between the two ES Robbins mats?
faq.a: The EverLife is 60 x 72 inches and rated for medium pile up to 3/4 inch. The Extra High Pile mat is 36 x 48 inches and rated for pile over 1 inch.

faq.q: Do glass mats need a pile rating?
faq.a: Glass stays rigid on top of the carpet, so it doesn't depend on cleats. Lorell lists its mat for any floor type; GLSLAND lists carpet or hard floor without a pile rating.

faq.q: How do I measure pile height?
faq.a: Push a ruler into the carpet to the backing and read the height of the fibers. If the carpet feels spongy because of thick padding, treat it as higher pile.

faq.q: How long does a rolled mat take to lie flat?
faq.a: Rolled mats need time to relax; about a day is a common guideline. The GORILLA GRIP and glass mats ship flat.

bottomLine: For low pile, the HON is the straightforward choice with a five-year warranty; the Anji Mountain is the alternative if the mat needs to look like a rug. For medium pile, the GORILLA GRIP covers a standard area and the ES Robbins EverLife a large one.

For extra-high or padded carpet, the ES Robbins Extra High Pile mat is the only rated option here. If you'd rather avoid pile ratings altogether, the Lorell and GLSLAND glass mats sit rigidly on top, with the MuArts as the heavy-load alternative.
